The expression has two main parts connected by `or`:
1. A complex nested logical expression (evaluates to False)
2. Another complex expression (evaluates to True)

The second part includes:
- `not not (The capital of Iraq is Baghdad.)` = `not not True` = `True`
- This TRUE value is part of an OR operation with other conditions
- Since we have `True or ...`, the whole right side evaluates to `True`
